svg.title: Mysa Home Assistant management coverage map
svg.desc: Integration and management: 35 of 45 implemented, 7 partial, 3 missing. Last reviewed 2026-10-12. Each tile represents one inventory row.
svg.text: Acceptance criteria for state, commands, lifecycle, managed workflows, and verification

g.text: State selection, command handling, lifecycle, workflows, and verification

rect.title: MGT-STATE-01 — Prefer a healthy local HomeKit temperature/action path; switch to cloud state when essential local reads fail. — Implemented

MGT-STATE-02 — Use cloud telemetry as fallback only when the thermostat is online and the measurement clock is fresh; make stale fallback values unavailable and recover on a fresh report. — Implemented
MGT-STATE-03 — Retain missing fields at their original observation age and let a successful independent source update without refreshing stale siblings. — Implemented
MGT-STATE-04 — Select each cloud field from valid reported observations using its own normalized source timestamp; reject invalid/future and desired-only values. — Implemented
MGT-STATE-05 — Track HTTPS humidity freshness independently from temperature and use it only when its own cloud observation is usable. — Implemented
MGT-STATE-06 — Select coherent paired limits and brightness from a single candidate source; do not mix a lone structured bound with an unrelated record bound. — Implemented
MGT-STATE-07 — Derive HVAC action from fresh reported stages/state bits; return unknown on missing or contradictory evidence instead of inferring action from selected mode. — Implemented
MGT-STATE-08 — Select the best applicable room-temperature source across local/cloud and any linked Mysa sensor, with explicit priority, freshness, and user-visible selection rules. — Partial

MGT-STATE-09 — Tolerate a device clock more than 24 hours ahead or behind using receipt-time-minus-five-minutes, with a per-device enabled default, diagnostics, and return to reported time after recovery. — Missing
MGT-STATE-10 — Keep connection status separate from measurement freshness: online must not make old readings fresh, and stale telemetry must not hide otherwise connected cloud settings. — Implemented

MGT-STATE-11 — Prefer valid MQTT humidity and numeric heating duty cycle while connected and less than 30 seconds old by local receipt time; expire each field independently and fall back to usable HTTPS observations without deriving numeric duty from a relay boolean. — Implemented
MGT-COMMAND-01 — Route supported writes locally first when HomeKit is healthy; avoid a cloud write after a successful local command. — Implemented
MGT-COMMAND-02 — For an uncertain local write, read back before cloud fallback; do not replay a rejected or already-applied command through a second path. — Implemented
MGT-COMMAND-03 — Serialize commands per thermostat and reassert the latest user intent after an older timed-out local write settles. — Implemented
MGT-COMMAND-04 — Keep accepted, ambiguous, stored, reported, unchanged, confirmed, and expired command outcomes distinct; never publish an accepted request as device state. — Implemented
MGT-COMMAND-05 — Bound cloud readback retries; do not resend an ambiguous write to another host or treat rate limiting as permission to replay. — Implemented
MGT-COMMAND-06 — Apply one capability-aware validation policy across climate commands, holds, schedules, and settings; validate every schedule event before mutating cloud state. — Partial
MGT-COMMAND-07 — On newer models, expose only advertised modes and controls; reject missing capabilities, unsupported model operations, and out-of-range targets. — Implemented
MGT-COMMAND-08 — Treat Central HVAC heat/cool AUTO as one validated mode update with both targets, mode-specific bounds, and minimum deadband; reject partial pairs before sending. — Implemented
MGT-COMMAND-09 — Convert Fahrenheit-facing HA commands and display steps consistently while preserving valid Celsius wire precision. — Implemented
MGT-COMMAND-10 — Show and send AC fan/swing operations only when the discovered remote supports those exact commands; hide them when off or unsupported. — Implemented
MGT-LIFECYCLE-01 — Share the HomeKit controller through HA runtime and stop it with the HA lifecycle. — Implemented
MGT-LIFECYCLE-02 — Keep polling available when subscriptions fail; close local sessions and cancel refresh/reconciliation work on unload. — Implemented
MGT-LIFECYCLE-03 — Mark the local path unavailable on failed/missing essential reads, but tolerate optional-field failures; an error notification cannot restore health by itself. — Implemented

MGT-LIFECYCLE-04 — Refresh HomeKit characteristic addresses, supported modes, ranges, and subscriptions on configuration changes/reconnects, with bounded retry and stale-field removal. Consume the refresh in HA on reconnect and a 15-minute backstop, rerun capability discovery, and keep polling when subscriptions fail without duplicate listeners or refresh loops. — Implemented

MGT-LIFECYCLE-05 — After an offline local-only start, publish newly discovered capability entities once local recovery succeeds; remove listeners on unload and avoid duplicate entities on repeated recovery. — Implemented
MGT-LIFECYCLE-06 — Persist an accepted HomeKit pairing before further accessory reads and attempt bounded key cleanup if persistence fails. — Implemented

MGT-LIFECYCLE-07 — Preserve an interrupted HomeKit Device migration marker and retry without losing destination entities, entity IDs, or unrelated device metadata. Clear CONF_MIGRATE_FROM only after completion or when the source is already absent; cover failed unload, partial takeover, and retry. — Implemented
MGT-LIFECYCLE-08 — Journal schedule replacement/clear operations so failure, cancellation, shared attachments, app edits, and restart recovery do not lose unrelated schedules. — Implemented

MGT-LIFECYCLE-09 — Start MQTT without blocking HA setup, retry failed connections, renew live reporting after reconnect and before stream expiry, and cancel background work and close the client on unload. — Implemented
MGT-WORKFLOW-01 — Let the user add an already-enrolled account device and match local discovery to the correct cloud record without duplicating an existing device. — Implemented

MGT-WORKFLOW-02 — Gate entity creation on real capability data; do not default to heating controls when capabilities are missing, and create supported entities after later capability recovery. — Implemented
MGT-WORKFLOW-03 — Keep Climate Sensor read-only and prevent Central HVAC/Baseboard V3 from receiving legacy-only schedules, holds, heater configuration, and OTA entities. — Implemented
MGT-WORKFLOW-04 — Import app-enrolled newer devices through cloud account setup, clearly mark their support experimental, and avoid asking them for HomeKit pairing. — Implemented
MGT-WORKFLOW-05 — Recover account membership and pairing conflicts through explicit repair/setup steps without silently deleting or claiming another device. — Implemented
MGT-WORKFLOW-06 — Manage newer-model initial provisioning and fleet ownership end to end, including credential transfer, claim/finalization, and update lifecycle. — Missing
MGT-WORKFLOW-07 — Make experimental/support status and operational limits discoverable in device information and diagnostics without leaking account/device identifiers. — Implemented
MGT-WORKFLOW-08 — Remove a device with complete cleanup of its schedule attachments, shortcut actions, sensor links and group membership, preserving unrelated devices. — Partial

MGT-WORKFLOW-09 — Offer default-on global and per-device MQTT settings gated by cloud sign-in; persist device choices, subscribe/request only configured account-owned enabled devices, and avoid a connection when all devices are excluded. — Implemented

MGT-QUALITY-01 — On both observed Baseboard Lite devices, exercise local/cloud dual-source reads under healthy-local, local-unavailable, fresh-cloud, stale-cloud, and offline-cloud conditions; verify diagnostics identify the selected source and cloud observations remain available while HomeKit is active. — Partial

MGT-QUALITY-02 — Validate each remaining supported profile on matching hardware: non-Lite Baseboard generations, In-floor, Mini-Split AC, Baseboard V3, Central HVAC, and Climate Sensor. Confirm only applicable advertised controls appear, compare state and reversible writes with the Mysa app/device, and record model/firmware-specific exceptions. — Missing
MGT-QUALITY-03 — Explain and resolve the observed case where one Lite accepted cloud setpoint/OFF commands without a confirmed local change while another applied them. — Partial
MGT-QUALITY-04 — Verify an offered firmware release through trigger, status, installation, and installed-version transition on hardware. — Partial
MGT-QUALITY-05 — Calculate daily runtime/derived energy across spring-forward and fall-back transitions using elapsed UTC time while keeping local calendar-day boundaries. — Partial
MGT-QUALITY-06 — Expose enough source/age/request/command diagnostics to explain selected data and failures while redacting credentials and household identifiers. — Implemented

g.text: Each colored tile is one inventory row; group background is spacing and labeling only.

svg.text: Percentages are calculated independently within each panel; Partial rows remain visible and do not earn completion credit.
